name: Question 20
problem: In a medical clinic, a certain rapid test detects a particular infection. On average, $9$ out of every $300$ patients who take the test receive a positive result. Each patient’s test result is independent of the others. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that the nurse will test more than $6$ patients before seeing the first positive result is{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of patients tested until the first positive result is obtained. Since the chance that any single patient tests positive is $3%,$ the number of patients tested until the first positive result can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=\frac{9}{300}=0.03.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.03).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.03)^{x-1}(0.03) \\  & =(0.97)^{x-1}(0.03)\end{aligned}
$$

To compute $P(X>6),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X>6)=1-P(X\le 6)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 6) & =P(X\in {1,2,3,4,5,6}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4)+f(5)+f(6) \\  & =(0.97)^{1-1}(0.03)+(0.97)^{2-1}(0.03)+(0.97)^{3-1}(0.03) \\  & \,+(0.97)^{4-1}(0.03)+(0.97)^{5-1}(0.03)+(0.97)^{6-1}(0.03) \\  & =[1+(0.97)+(0.97)^{2}+(0.97)^{3}+(0.97)^{4}+(0.97)^{5}](0.03) \\  & ≈0.167,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability that the nurse will test more than $6$ patients before seeing the first positive result is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>6) & =1-P(X\le 6) \\  & ≈1-0.167 \\  & ≈0.833,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Let X be the number of patients tested until the first positive result is obtained. Since the chance that any single patient tests positive is 3%, the number of patients tested until the first positive result can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success p=9300=0.03.

So, X∼Geom(0.03). In this case, X has the following probability mass function: f(x)=(1−0.03)x−1(0.03)=(0.97)x−1(0.03)

To compute P(X>6), we will use the complement: P(X>6)=1−P(X≤6)

Computing the probability of the complement, we get P(X≤6)=P(X∈{1,2,3,4,5,6})=f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4)+f(5)+f(6)=(0.97)1−1(0.03)+(0.97)2−1(0.03)+(0.97)3−1(0.03)+(0.97)4−1(0.03)+(0.97)5−1(0.03)+(0.97)6−1(0.03)=[1+(0.97)+(0.97)2+(0.97)3+(0.97)4+(0.97)5](0.03)≈0.167, rounded to 3 decimal places.

Therefore, the probability that the nurse will test more than 6 patients before seeing the first positive result is P(X>6)=1−P(X≤6)≈1−0.167≈0.833, rounded to 3 decimal places.
